items.summary: Create a useFocusMonitor React hook that tracks page visibility changes using the Page Visibility API (visibilitychange event) and window focus/blur events (window.onblur and window.onfocus), recording timestamps whenever the user leaves and returns to the page

In the useFocusMonitor hook, calculate how long the user stayed away from the page by comparing leave and return timestamps, and count how many times the user switches away within a time period (e.g., per minute)

In the useFocusMonitor hook, implement a distraction score calculation that updates when the user switches tabs frequently (e.g., more than 5 times in 2 minutes), incrementing the score based on switching frequency

Display a small on-screen warning component when the distraction score threshold is exceeded, showing a message like 'Frequent tab switching detected. Try focusing for a few minutes.' with dismissible functionality

Send the distraction score and switching statistics (tab switch count, time away, timestamps) to the backend using a POST request to an API endpoint, transmitting data in JSON format whenever significant changes occur

Create a backend Motoko function to record focus monitoring data including distraction score, tab switch count, time away from page, and timestamp, storing this data in the existing backend storage structure

Add inline code comments to the useFocusMonitor hook explaining each section including event listener setup, timestamp recording, duration calculation, switch counting, distraction score logic, and API communication, ensuring the code is beginner-friendly and modifiable
